exposure: methylation status of 96 single genes linked to T cell activation, cytokine production, inflammatory response, and stem cell transcription
Mode of delivery (elective cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Methylation status of 96 single genes linked to T cell activation, cytokine production, inflammatory response, and stem cell transcription
cohort: 41 newborn infants (23 vaginal delivery, 18 elective cesarean section) for global DNA methylation analysis and 48 newborn infants (20 vaginal delivery, 28 elective cesarean section) for single gene methylation analysis
finding: While no difference in global methylation was observed, methylation of single genes (ELA2 and IRF1) was significantly higher in infants delivered by elective cesarean section compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Methylation of single genes (ELA2 and IRF1) was significantly higher in infants delivered by elective cesarean section compared to vaginal delivery.
